input.quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.
input.rationale: The only liability limitation in the Agreement (p0077, inside the indemnity section) caps TrueLink alone at 12 months' hosting and support compensation, while Client's liability — including the very broad Section 12(a) indemnity — remains unlimited. That is walk-away territory under the rule (Customer uncapped while Vendor capped), and the sole carve-out covers only TrueLink's gross negligence and wilful misconduct, with nothing for indemnification or confidentiality (Section 10). We therefore target the fallback with the smallest edit: "TRUELINK'S LIABILITY" becomes "EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY" so the cap binds both parties, and the parenthetical carve-out is made mutual and extended to indemnification obligations and breach of confidentiality obligations. The existing Section 3, 4, 7 and 11 scope and the 12-month compensation basis are retained verbatim, so TrueLink gains no new cap protection for matters (e.g. warranties, service performance) where it is presently uncapped. Preferred items not pressed here: the USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid or payable", anchoring the window to the event giving rise to the claim, a mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud and IP infringement, and the payment-obligations exclusion.

proposal.summary: Make the existing Section 3/4/7/11 12-month fee cap mutual and carve out indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is a mutual cap of 12 months' fees with indemnification, confidentiality breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap; as drafted the cap protects only TrueLink and leaves Client's liability unlimited. We have made the same cap apply to both parties and carved those obligations out, leaving the existing section scope and fee basis untouched.
